newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Amplico leads life insurers in net growth.
newsitem.headline: Polish Amplico leads life insurers in net growth.

text.p: Among Polish life insurers Amplico Life and Commercial Union reported the fastest growth of net profit in the first three quarters of 1996, a poll by the Nowa Europa daily showed.
It said Amplico, Compensa and Hestia Insurance were at the top of non-life insurers with fastest growth of net profit.
It said Amplico Life reported a net profit of 140.8 million zlotys in the first nine months of 1996, up 52.8 million from corresponding period last year.
Amplico is 55-percent owned by American International Group Inc (AIG) and 45-percent by Polish state-owned bank Pekao SA.
Commercial Union, a subsidary of Britain's Commercial Union Plc, had a net profit of 212.2 million zlotys in the three quarters, up from 75.8 million last year.

Non-life Amplico insurer showed a net profit of 3.5 million zlotys, up from last year's 0.4 million, while Compensa, a subsidary of Mostostal Export, earned 1.3 million, against 20,000 zlotys last year.
Hestia Insurance, a subsidary of the German insurer Alte Leipziger Europa, had a net of 3.2 million zlotys in the three quarters of 1996, up from 0.2 million last year.

The daily said the Polish state-owned Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU) maintained its high market share among the non-life companies at 67.8 percent, with Warta ranking second with 14.1 percent of the market.
Polisa was third with 3.5 percent and Hestia Insurance fourth with 3.4 percent.

It said among life-insurers PZU Zycie, a subsidary of PZU saw its market share reduced to 77.6 percent from 87.2 percent last year, but remained the leader with Commercial Union ranking second with 10.7 percent of the market.
Amplico Life was third with 7.1 percent of the market.
